passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report. The following discussion may contain forward-looking statements that reflect our plans, estimates, and beliefs. Our actual results could differ materially from those discussed in these forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause or contribute to these differences include those factors discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report, particularly in “Part I. Item 1A. Risk Factors” and “Forward-Looking Information.” Our Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in U.S. dollars, in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. (“GAAP”). Discussion of our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2026 compared to fiscal 2025 is presented below. Discussion of our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024 can be found in “Part II. Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in our Annual Report for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2025. The following discussion includes organic net sales growth (decline) which is a non-GAAP financial measure. See “Non-GAAP Financial Measure” for additional information regarding this measure. 25 Table of Contents Overview We are a global industrial technology leader creating a safer, sustainable, productive, and connected future. As a trusted innovation partner, our broad range of connectivity and sensor solutions enable the distribution of power, signal, and data to advance next-generation transportation, energy networks, automated factories, data centers enabling artificial intelligence, and more. Change in Place of Incorporation On September 30, 2024, TE Connectivity Ltd., our former parent entity, merged with and into TE Connectivity plc, a public limited company incorporated under Irish law and the surviving entity, in order to effect our change in jurisdiction of incorporation from Switzerland to Ireland. Effective beginning in fiscal 2025, we are organized under the laws of Ireland. Summary of Fiscal 2026 Performance ● Our fiscal 2026 net sales increased 15.2% from fiscal 2025 due to sales growth in both the Industrial Solutions and Transportation Solutions segments. On an organic basis, our net sales increased 11.9% in fiscal 2026 as compared to fiscal 2025. ● Our net sales by segment were as follows: ● Transportation Solutions —Our net sales increased 7.3% in fiscal 2026 due to sales increases in the automotive and commercial transportation end markets. ● Industrial Solutions —Our net sales increased 25.8% in fiscal 2026 primarily as a result of sales growth in the digital data networks; energy; automation and connected living; and aerospace, defense, and marine end markets. ● We paid cash dividends to shareholders of $2.98 per ordinary share in fiscal 2026. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below, that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and the trading price of our securities. These risks are not the only ones facing us. Our business is also subject to general risks that affect many other companies. Additional risks not currently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial may also impair our business operations, financial condition, and liquidity . 7 Table of Contents Risks Relating to the Macroeconomic Environment and Our Global Presence Conditions in global or regional economies, capital and money markets, and banking systems, and cyclical industry demand may adversely affect our results of operations, financial position, and cash flows. Our business and operating results have been and will continue to be affected by economic conditions regionally or globally, including new or increasing tariffs and other barriers to trade, including ongoing trade and tariff tensions between the United States (“U.S.”), China, the EU, and other countries, changes to fiscal and monetary policy, inflation or deflation, slower growth or recession, higher interest rates, labor disruptions, the cost and availability of consumer and business credit, end demand from consumer and industrial markets, significant bank failures, government shutdowns, and concerns as to sovereign debt levels including credit rating downgrades and defaults on sovereign debt. Any of these economic factors could cause our customers to experience deterioration of their businesses, cash flow, financial condition, and ability to obtain financing. As a result, existing or potential customers may delay or cancel plans to purchase our products and may not be able to fulfill their obligations to us in a timely fashion or in full. Further, our vendors may experience similar problems, which may impact their ability to fulfill our orders or meet agreed service and quality levels. If regional or global economic conditions deteriorate, our results of operations, financial position, and cash flows could be materially adversely affected. Also, deterioration in economic conditions, expectations for future revenue, projected future cash flows, or other factors have triggered and could trigger additional recognition of impairment charges for our goodwill or other long-lived assets. Impairment charges, if any, may be material to our results of operations and financial position. Foreign currency exchange rates may adversely affect our results. Our Consolidated Financial Statements are prepared in U.S. dollars; however, many of our non-U.S. operations have a functional currency other than the U.S. dollar, and their results are translated into U.S. dollars for reporting purposes. Changes in the relative values of currencies may have a significant effect on our results of operations, financial position, and cash flows. We are exposed to the effects of changes in foreign currency exchange rates on our costs and revenue. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure plus shareholder distributions, leaving a sizeable residual buffer after dividends and buybacks. This internally funded profile reduces reliance on external borrowing for routine cash uses and supports the minimal indicative financial risk profile.

Gross and net leverage both sit well below the Industrials sector median and improved year on year, reflecting debt held broadly flat while EBITDA expanded. Interest coverage is a multiple of the sector median, underscoring substantial headroom against the next risk-band boundary.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows meaningful senior notes maturing within the next few years alongside a commercial paper balance, so refinancing and rollover risk is recurring rather than remote. A new revolving facility refinanced the prior agreement, but access to money markets remains a dependency for short-term paper.

Risk factors flag tariff and trade tensions, foreign currency translation exposure given most sales invoiced in non-U.S. dollar currencies, and cyclical end demand. These could pressure revenue and cash flow, and deterioration could trigger goodwill or long-lived asset impairment charges material to results.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow relative to debt is roughly double the sector median and improved year on year, while operating cash flow to debt also exceeds the peer median. This indicates debt service is comfortably funded from internally generated cash rather than refinancing.

The current ratio exceeds both the prior year and the sector median, and cash balances provide a partial offset to gross debt. Liquidity therefore appears adequate to meet near-term maturities without stressing the balance sheet.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with leverage and cash-flow coverage both in the strongest tier and comfortably clear of the next threshold. Operating margin exceeds the sector median and improved year on year, supporting the view that earnings quality underpins debt capacity.

Our forward view is that shareholder returns absorb a large share of free cash flow, so deleveraging depends on continued EBITDA growth rather than retained cash. Sustained tariff pressure or currency headwinds could slow that growth, but current headroom leaves ample cushion before any risk-band migration.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流充裕覆蓋資本開支加股東分派，於股息及回購後仍留有相當大的剩餘緩衝。此內部融資模式減少對外部借貸的依賴以應付日常現金用途，並支持最低的指示性財務風險狀況。
總槓桿及淨槓桿均遠低於工業行業中位數，並按年改善，反映債務大致持平而EBITDA擴張。利息覆蓋率為行業中位數的倍數，凸顯相對於下一個風險區間界限有充裕空間。

key_risks.text: 債務附註顯示未來數年內有相當金額的高級票據到期，同時存在商業票據餘額，故再融資及展期風險屬經常性而非遙遠。新循環融資額度為先前協議再融資，但短期票據仍依賴貨幣市場准入。
風險因素指出關稅及貿易緊張、外匯折算風險（因大部分銷售以非美元貨幣開票）以及週期性終端需求。此等因素可能對收入及現金流構成壓力，而惡化可能觸發對業績有重大影響的商譽或長期資產減值費用。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流相對債務約為行業中位數的兩倍，並按年改善，而營運現金流相對債務亦高於同業中位數。此表明債務償付由內部產生現金充裕支持，而非依賴再融資。
流動比率高於去年及行業中位數，而現金餘額對總債務提供部分抵銷。因此流動性似乎足以應付近期到期債務而不對資產負債表構成壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人呈現最低的指示性財務風險狀況，槓桿及現金流覆蓋均處於最強級別，並穩妥地遠離下一個門檻。營運利潤率超過行業中位數並按年改善，支持盈利質量支撐債務能力的觀點。
我們的前瞻觀點是股東回報佔用大部分自由現金流，故去槓桿取決於EBITDA持續增長而非留存現金。持續關稅壓力或貨幣逆風可能減慢該增長，但當前空間在任何風險區間遷移前留有充足緩衝。
